title: State Proposition 47 treatment grants to the City: each objective as scored
question: The State corrections board paid the City two $6 million Proposition 47 grants for treatment beds and case management. Which objectives did the City's own evaluator score as met?
finding: Of 17 objectives in the two final evaluations, 8 were not met, almost met, not reported or had no data. The grant-funded treatment beds ran well below the 90% occupancy target (Cohort 1: 66% against a 90% target; Cohort 2: 47% against a 90% target). A recidivism objective in the first grant was scored 'met' on six people with a prior conviction.
how: Each final evaluation's objectives table was read line by line: objective number and wording, the evaluator's status, and the first 25 words of the evaluator's note. Grant size and period are read from each report's background section.
limits: In the objective wording, SUD means substance use disorder, MH mental health and CASC the Community Assessment and Services Center. The evaluations were commissioned by the grantee (the health department), as the State requires; they are self-assessments. Occupancy fell in the COVID-19 period, and the evaluator also notes slow referrals and a late start; empty beds may still have been paid for as reserved capacity, which the reports do not say. The State board's own grant monitoring is not in these files.
